title: Perplexity and Intelligence
body: November 22, 2026 Research Safety Perplexity and Intelligence By Jakub Pachocki, Chief Scientist at OpenAI Share From afar, it might seem like modern AI is built similarly to how software has been built in previous decades: with a diverse set of techniques targeting specific capabilities. There are indeed a variety of methods, but rather than designing something from scratch, they are mostly harnessing the intelligence coming from a much simpler and less interpretable process: training a compressor (or, equivalently ⁠ (opens in a new window) , predictor) on a very large corpus of data. 1 I believe tracking the pace of progress on training better compressors is key to understanding the arc of advances in AI. In this post, I argue for establishing perplexity (or, equivalently, cross-entropy loss) as a metric to compare between model developers and inform shared safety standards. As a first step, I provide more transparency into pretraining progress at OpenAI. Publishing our internal perplexity measurements took some consideration; it gives competitors a clearer picture of where we stand, but that concern is outweighed by the urgency of establishing shared ⁠ (opens in a new window) safety measures across the industry. We at OpenAI hope for this to be a step towards building a shared scientific basis for future pacing efforts. A simplified, but fundamentally informative, view of AI development is that first, one builds a large computer, then uses it to pretrain a model (compressor) on a large unstructured dataset, then applies a variety of techniques—like prompting, finetuning or reinforcement learning—in different contexts to elicit the latent capabilities of that model. Algorithmic progress can blur the distinction between training phases, but we can still separate the creation of the AI with hard-to-predict emergent capabilities (which I earlier dubbed “ an alien mind ⁠ ”) and the subsequent targeted elicitation. The primary way we measure progress on this key “intelligence substrate” has remained remarkably constant over the years—we have been tracking the perplexity of the models on a held-out dataset. 2 , 3 Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token on average; lower perplexity means better predictions. The plot opening this blog post shows how this metric evolved for our models starting with GPT‑3.5. The range of capabilities of models that are largely described by this one metric is stunning. Setting the new perplexity state-of-the-art on older datasets 4 , GPT‑2 was arguably the first model capable of consistently formulating coherent paragraphs of text. The next major leap, GPT‑3, was capable of learning in context, given a few examples of a task. GPT‑3.5, at a log-perplexity of ~0.99 on our current main evaluation dataset, was capable of fluent conversation and formed the basis for the original ChatGPT. GPT‑4, at ~0.91, was proficient at utilizing chain-of-thought reasoning productively, which motivated the subsequent targeted elicitation of this capability and the creation of modern reasoning models. Now, as we have reached losses below 0.8, we have seen the emergence of transformative capabilities in fields like cybersecurity and mathematics. I want to reemphasize that it was not at all clear a priori that these capabilities would appear once those precise perplexity thresholds are met—they can fundamentally be seen as emergent latent capabilities from progress on this one metric. As AI advances very rapidly, the scope and way in which we measure downstream capabilities may change quickly. It would make little sense to evaluate GPT‑2 and GPT‑3 on most modern benchmarks; and the benchmarks used then were largely saturated around GPT‑4. In contrast, I believe looking at progress on pretraining is likely to stay informative. A particular change in the pace of progress comes from the increasing contribution of AI to its own development. The most commonly discussed metrics revolve around AI augmenting and replacing human researchers in all stages of the development cycle; with an ultimate inflection point seen at “full recursive self-improvement”, where the process would be entirely automated with no human oversight. Apart from considering such a state as something we should obviously avoid for the sake of maintaining human control, I find this general framing misses something crucial. There is a potential step change that may come from AI participation in one key part of the development process: algorithmic research on pretraining. We have recently witnessed unprecedented acceleration in another domain. For more than a year, we have been posing open problems in mathematics to our models as one of the ways of evaluating them. Once we upgraded to a model of log-perplexity ~0.76, it started producing groundbreaking results. For many of us that have previously worked in mathematics and adjacent fields, seeing the resolutions to questions we’ve long thought about coming out of the model one after another in a single Slack thread felt deeply surreal. Having experienced that allows us to extrapolate—such a sudden transformation is plausible in deep learning research too. While this field relies more on experimentation, there is a long history of simple insights being missed for years; and so as soon as 2027 we could conceivably see a similar avalanche of fundamental pretraining advancements 5 . While I expect AI will also significantly contribute to progress on alignment and monitoring, I think that progress is unlikely to be fast enough to allow the full potential acceleration in pretraining. Given that the main way new surprising capabilities emerge is by progress on compression, a measure rooted in perplexity could give us a shared benchmark for general intelligence, regardless of the degree of automation of the development process. Extrapolating from recent progress, we should expect further transformative capabilities as we enter the ~0.68-0.7 log-perplexity window. I don’t know what those capabilities will be, and we may not be testing for them today. At the same time, we should also expect further degradation ⁠ (opens in a new window) in currently dominant forms of alignment auditing and further increases in evaluation and training awareness. I believe frontier model developers should jointly endeavour to establish shared norms for how to evaluate such models and red-team safety cases for them by the time they are first used, including shared transparency standards. I further propose common limits , based on perplexity and other measurements, that developers are committed to not crossing until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone (such as the development of a successor to CoT monitors). That is, I’d like an industry standard that specifies a first limit on development, measured by some key metric we can track across labs, and what concretely we’d need to achieve before going beyond it. I hope that this leads the way to a common framework for setting successive limits and pacing further development. Perplexity as a shared metric has challenges: Difficulty of comparison across labs. Different developers use different evaluation datasets and train on different data mixtures. Here, we report the numbers on the main dataset we have been tracking; I believe if we establish a goal of transparency we can find transferable ways to compare the quality of different base models. Detachment from actionable evaluations. Perplexity does not directly correspond to a task we care about. The reason to care about it is that we can expect advances on it to lead to emergence of entirely new capabilities. Not accounting for advances outside of pretraining. Most notably, chain-of-thought reasoning does not reduce perplexity achieved by the model, even though it leads to a drastic increase in capabilities. Unknown floor. We do not expect it is possible to achieve a loss of 0, which would correspond to being able to predict the dataset entirely deterministically. But we do not know what the inherent entropy of the data is. As we approach it, the apparent progress on perplexity will slow, but smaller gains on perplexity will correspond to larger leaps in model intelligence. At the same time, perplexity has stood the test of time as a metric many research teams have put a lot of effort into optimizing, and it continues to deliver consistent gains on general intelligence. I believe it can play an important role in standardizing how we talk about AI progress, and hope to see more transparency about it across the industry. Compute Scaling Ethics & Safety 2026 Author Jakub Pachocki Footnotes 1 It’s important to note that “compressor” in this sense is something that is capable of performing compression by predicting unseen data, not a compressed artifact like a GZIP file - that is, the best compressor trained on a given corpus does not necessarily “remember” the contents of the corpus. 2 In practice, we generally track the log of perplexity, also called cross-entropy loss . 3 The primary held-out datasets we’ve been using since GPT-3.5 are sourced from our internal codebase, and those are the numbers reported here (for a fixed snapshot). 4 Given what GPT‑2 and GPT‑3 were trained on, how well they predict code is a poor proxy for their general capabilities. This showcases a potential challenge arising from dataset selection with using perplexity as a shared metric; however it should still be informative to evaluate them jointly with modern models on general text. I chose to report perplexity on our internal codebase because I wanted to share the numbers we rely on most today to gauge progress in pretraining at OpenAI. 5 On the plot of losses of OpenAI models, you can see a steep acceleration in 2026. We attribute it mostly to the outcomes of long term research and compute investments, and only in a smaller part to automation. However, for the most recent models, we have already seen meaningful design contributions coming from AI ⁠ . title: Senior Leader of the Sinaloa Cartel and One of FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives Arrested in Mexico Following a Homeland Security Task Force Investigation
body: Press Release Senior Leader of the Sinaloa Cartel and One of FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives Arrested in Mexico Following a Homeland Security Task Force Investigation Saturday, November 21, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs OAG Fausto Isidro Meza Flores , also known as “Chapo Isidro,” an alleged leader of the Sinaloa Cartel, has been captured by the Mexican military following a Homeland Security Task Force Investigation. “We commend Mexico’s military and special forces on last night’s capture of Sinaloa Cartel senior leader ‘Chapo Isidro,’ said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “A combined interagency effort, including the Homeland Security Task Force, supported this Mexican operation to remove a leader of one of the most dangerous drug cartels in Mexico. This successful operation is the result of a bilateral effort to eliminate terrorists in Mexico. We extend our condolences to the families of the elite soldiers who were killed and our gratitude to the Mexican government.” “The arrest of Chapo Isidro demonstrates the outstanding strength and reach of the Homeland Security Task Force,” said Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin. “Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) and our HSTF partners relentlessly pursued one of the world’s most dangerous cartel leaders, whose organization is alleged to have flooded our communities with deadly narcotics and terrorized communities through extreme violence. This operation sends an unmistakable message, cartel leaders cannot hide behind borders, money, or brutality. The Homeland Security Task Force will continue its work to dismantle these criminal and terrorist networks, hold their leaders accountable, and protect the American people.” Meza Flores was captured on November 20 in a spectacular military operation in Guasave, Sinaloa, Mexico, that also resulted in the arrest of alleged cartel leader German Rolando Galvez Meza, also known as “El Serafin.” A federal grand jury in the District of Columbia returned a second superseding indictment on September 25 charging Meza-Flores, 44, of Sonora, Mexico, with conspiracy to provide material support to a terrorist organization, narcoterrorism, conducting a continuing criminal enterprise, money laundering and firearms related charges. The case is being prosecuted by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of California and the Justice Department’s Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section. The Sinaloa Cartel is one of the most prolific and dangerous drug cartels in Mexico, known for its widespread use of corruption and violence to further its drug trafficking activities. On February 20, 2025, the U.S. Secretary of State designated the Cartel de Sinaloa as a Foreign Terrorist Organization (FTO) under Section 219 of the Immigration and Nationality Act and as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist under Executive Order 13224. The Secretary of State has also listed the following aliases for the Cartel de Sinaloa: Sinaloa Cartel, Mexican Federation, and Guadalajara Cartel. According to court documents, under Meza Flores’s leadership, the Sinaloa Cartel produced and trafficked multi-tonnage quantities of drugs, including cocaine, methamphetamine, heroin, marijuana, and fentanyl into the United States, and used extreme violence to further its operations. Meza Flores commanded a large contingent of gunmen to control significant territory in the Guasave, Los Mochis, and remote Sinaloa mountains. The cartel uses this territory to manufacture and distribute illicit controlled substances, transporting them north to the United States. It is further alleged that Meza Flores has engaged in continual and extreme violence, including (1) murdering rival cartel members in public; (2) kidnapping, torturing, and murdering rival cartel members at camps and elsewhere; (3) kidnapping, torturing, and murdering members of the Mexican police; and (4) terrorizing the people of Mexico. “Meza Flores is on the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives List for a reason; he is the most dangerous man in Mexico,” said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “For decades Meza Flores has promoted the terrorist objectives of the Sinaloa Cartel, promoting unparalleled violence throughout southern Mexico and flooding the United States with deadly substances all in the name of profit. With this indictment made possible by the Homeland Security Task Force, subsequent arrest and the continued support of our Mexican partners, we aim to bring him to justice and fully dismantle this cartel.” “Chapo Isidro built an empire in the shadows. Today’s sunrise was his sunset,” said U.S. Attorney Adam Gordon for the Southern District of California. “Another FBI Ten Most Wanted fugitive is off the board,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro,” has been captured by Mexican forces with U.S. assistance. This alleged cartel leader is accused of flooding American communities with deadly drugs, including fentanyl. This is the 11th Ten Most Wanted fugitive captured under the Trump Administration. Outstanding work by our law enforcement partners in Mexico and everyone involved in this operation. Under President Trump’s leadership, this FBI will continue relentlessly pursuing the criminals and cartels poisoning our communities and threatening American lives.” “Homeland Security Investigations is proud of the exceptional work of our special agents and personnel across our domestic and international offices whose determination, expertise, and coordination through the HSTF helped bring Chapo Isidro to justice,” said HSI Acting Executive Associate Director John A. Condon. “Working alongside our HSTF partners, HSI investigated this dangerous cartel leader and helped dismantle the criminal enterprise he allegedly used to poison American communities and fuel brutal violence. This arrest demonstrates the reach of HSI’s global investigative authorities and the strength of the HSTF as partners work together to take coordinated and relentless action against transnational criminal organizations that threaten our homeland.” Meza Flores is charged in a six-count superseding indictment filed in the District of Columbia with leading a continuing criminal enterprise, conspiracy to manufacture and distribute cocaine, methamphetamine, heroin, marijuana, and fentanyl for importation into the United States, international money laundering conspiracy, conspiracy to provide material support to a terrorist organization, narcoterrorism, and using a firearm including a machinegun and a destructive device. If convicted of these charges, Meza Flores faces the death penalty or a mandatory term of life in prison. The U.S. Department of State is offering a reward of up to $5 million for information that led to the arrest and/or will lead to the conviction of Chapo Isidro. If you have any information concerning Chapo Isidro, please contact your local FBI office or the nearest American Embassy or Consulate or call the FBI at 1-800-CALL-FBI (1-800-225-5324). You can also submit a tip online at tips.fbi.gov See: https://www.state.gov/fausto-isidro-meza-flores The HSTF including FBI Washington and San Diego Field Offices and HSI San Diego investigated the case with significant assistance from DEA, ATF, and the U.S. Marshals Service. Deputy Chief James Hepburn and Trial Attorney Jayce Born of the Criminal Division’s Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section (MNF) and Assistant U.S. Attorney Joshua Mellor of the Southern District of California are prosecuting the case. The Justice Department's National Security Division, Office of International Affairs and Capital Case Section provided significant assistance. The Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section’s (MNF) mission is to take the profit out of crime, eliminate drug cartels, and protect the U.S. financial system. MNF pursues criminal prosecutions and criminal and civil asset recovery actions involving: financial facilitators who launder profits for criminals; financial institutions and their officers and employees whose actions threaten the U.S. financial system and financial institutions; international money launderers who support transnational organized crime; and the top command and control of international drug trafficking organizations. MNF’s Narcotic and Dangerous Drug Unit investigates and prosecutes the top command and control elements of international drug cartels, drug trafficking organizations, and related transnational criminal organizations. This case is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of U.S. law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. Updated November 21, 2026 Topic Homeland Security Task Force Component Office of the Attorney General Press Release Number: 26-1395

body:

Main Menu Toggle Button Sections Search Toggle Button Search Search Submit Button Submit Home News & Events Press Releases Press Release November 20, 2026 Federal Reserve announces College Fed Challenge winners For release at 4:15 p.m. EST Share The University of California, Los Angeles won the 23rd Annual National College Fed Challenge. The University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) won the 23rd annual national College Fed Challenge on Friday, a team competition that encourages undergraduate students to learn about the U.S. economy, monetary policymaking, and the role of the Federal Reserve System. Teams analyze economic and financial conditions and formulate a monetary policy recommendation, modeling the Federal Open Market Committee. The team, from Los Angeles, California, represented the San Francisco District and included Aarushi Maheshwari, Annika Chan, Atul Prasanth, Caitlyn Cox, Finn Karish, Eli Brooks (alternate), Kennedy Yang (alternate), Manasi Vartak (alternate), Ronojoy Borpujari (alternate), and Sahil Sudani (alternate). The team's advisers were Chris Surro and Ali Haider Ismail. "I am very happy to congratulate the students who competed in this year's College Fed Challenge, especially the winners and finalists," said Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh. "They took on the same big questions we policymakers face. I'm impressed by their talent, their rigor, and their eagerness to think hard about monetary policy and the economy." This year's College Fed Challenge included 141 schools from 34 states across the nation, the most in the competition's history. Teams submitted video presentations or participated in local competitions last month. Twenty-one semi-finalist teams then participated in question-and-answer sessions held earlier this month, and seven finalists were invited to the Federal Reserve Board for the national finals. The other national finalists were the University of Chicago in second place and the University of Maryland, College Park in third place. Teams with honorable mentions include Cleveland State University, Harvard College, Pennsylvania State University, and St. Lawrence University. Teams were evaluated on their economic analysis, responses to the judges' questions, teamwork, and presentations. For media inquiries, please email [email protected] or call 202-452-2955. Last Update:
            November 20, 2026

title: Operation Economic Outcast Targets Corrupt Regime Insiders Exploiting Iran’s Oil Sector for Personal Gain
body: November 20, 2026 WASHINGTON —Today, as part of Operation Economic Outcast, the U.S. Department of the Treasury is targeting key “oil trustees” the Iranian regime relies on to facilitate the sale of oil abroad. With no oil on the water outside of the U.S. military blockade and no oil loaded onto vessels since the start of Operation Economic Outcast, the regime is attempting to recoup billions of dollars from its oil trustees.  In many cases, these corrupt trustees have kept the oil revenue for personal gain. “Iran’s tyrannical regime never fails to put its own interests before those of its own citizens, even as ordinary Iranians face shortages of bread and fuel,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent .  “The regime has exhausted its seaborne oil supply, and it may never see the revenue from the oil it has already sold. The ship is sinking.” The designations imposed today are being taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13902, which targets the Iranian petroleum, petrochemical, and aviation sectors, among other key sectors of the Iranian economy, and E.O. 13224, as amended, a counterterrorism authority. OPERATION ECONOMIC OUTCAST IS ISOLATING THE IRANIAN REGIME Announced by Secretary Bessent on August 24, 2026, dubbed Economic D-Day , Operation Economic Outcast is severing the remaining economic lifelines that sustain the Iranian regime.  Treasury has mapped the networks, facilitators, and financial channels that Iran uses to smuggle oil, evade sanctions, and fund terror.  Working with partners across the U.S. government, the European Union, United Kingdom, Gulf partners, and others, Treasury is targeting any source of the regime’s illicit revenue, as well as its sanctions evasion schemes to move funds. Operation Economic Outcast has significantly expanded sanctions risk for those who continue to choose to do business with Iran.  Treasury warned that any entity facilitating money laundering or sanctions evasion on behalf of Iran risks being cut off from the U.S. financial system. Operation Economic Outcast has also expanded sanctions exposure for non-U.S. persons who continue doing business with the Iranian regime and will accelerate the pace of U.S. enforcement. More information on Operation Economic Outcast is available here . UNTRUSTWORTHY TRUSTEES Mohammad Javad Bavand (Bavand) and Majid Taj (Taj), the brother of the Iranian Football Federation’s president, operate as part of a network of regime insiders tasked with obtaining desperately needed cash by selling from Iran’s dwindling oil reserves.  Bavand, a former IRGC intelligence officer, has spearheaded this effort, entrusting a group of personal contacts, including Taj, to recoup Iran’s oil funds located in third countries.  The Iranian regime continues to entrust Bavand and Taj’s network with facilitating Iran’s oil sales, despite members owing billions of dollars to the regime from previous sales.  Bavand has worked with a variety of illicit oil trading actors, including the IRGC and Sepehr Energy Jahan Nama Pars Company (SEJ), a U.S.-designated front company tasked with selling oil for the Iranian Armed Forces General Staff. Mohammad Javad Bavand and Majid Taj are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13902 for operating in the petroleum sector of the Iranian economy. REGIME FACILITATORS Mohammadhossein Servati (Servati), the son of IRGC Brigadier General Mohsen Servati, has held executive positions at companies operated by SEJ, including SEJ front company Xin Rui Jin Trad Co., Limited , and Sepehr Energy Hamta Pars , a subsidiary of SEJ.  Xin Rui Jin Trad Co., Limited brokered and received shipments of Iranian oil on behalf of SEJ for delivery to Chinese teapot refineries. Mohammadhossein Servati is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Sepehr Energy Jahan Nama Pars Company. Mojtaba Arabnejad (Mojtaba) is the son of the designated Iranian businessman and CEO of Iran’s Mahan Air , Hamid Arabnejad .  Using his familial ties and special connections with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force (IRGC-QF), Mojtaba has been involved in purchasing aircraft parts for Mahan Air and procuring weapons for the Iranian military under the auspices of agricultural companies.  Like others designated today, Mojtaba has overseen oil sales for the Iranian regime, the proceeds from which have supported Mahan Air. Mojtaba Arabnejad is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Mahan Air. SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions, unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of blocked persons. Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis. OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades or conspires to violate U.S. sanctions.  Individuals located in the United States or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000.  Financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities with designated or otherwise blocked persons, including the persons designated today.  This includes, in addition to blocking prohibitions, that OFAC can prohibit or impose strict conditions on opening or maintaining, in the United States, a correspondent account or a payable-through account of a foreign financial institution that knowingly conducts or facilitates any significant transaction on behalf of a person who is designated pursuant to the relevant authority. The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the SDN List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List, when consistent with relevant statutes and other authorities.  The ultimate goal of sanctions is to bring about a positive change in behavior.  What constitutes a sufficient change in circumstance will vary based on context, including the status of the broader geopolitical circumstances affecting the national security and foreign policy interests implicated by the declared national emergency.  In the case of sanctions related to Iran, OFAC is employing all available statutory, regulatory, and policy tools to resolve the persistent national emergencies posed by Iran, which has not changed its behavior to align with U.S. national security and foreign policy objectives.  OFAC sanctions determinations, including removal determinations, are made consistent with Administration foreign policy and national security policies and priorities.  For more information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on How to Request Removal from an OFAC List. Click here for more information on today’s action. ###

title: Treasury Sanctions Major Drug Trafficking Organizations Supporting Terrorist Cartels
body: November 19, 2026 Coordinated Action with International Partners Targets a Cartel-Linked Outlaw Motorcycle Gang and Canadian-Based Mafia Leaders and Facilitators WASHINGTON —Today, the Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned two international drug trafficking organizations: the Australia-headquartered Comanchero Outlaw Motorcycle Gang ( Comancheros ) and the Italy-based ‘Ndrangheta , a mafia-type criminal syndicate.  By providing essential logistical and operational support, the Comancheros and ‘Ndrangheta help terrorist cartels expand their international reach and sustain global narcotrafficking networks. “Cartels do not operate in isolation. They rely on other criminal organizations like the Comancheros and ‘Ndrangheta to move drugs, launder illicit proceeds, and ultimately poison Americans with narcotics,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent .  “Treasury will continue to expose and disrupt narcoterrorism networks to Keep America Safe.” The Comancheros and the ‘Ndrangheta operate sophisticated transnational criminal networks that facilitate large-scale drug trafficking and money laundering. The ‘Ndrangheta controls a significant share of the European cocaine trade, while the Comancheros have helped open access to some of the world's most lucrative illicit drug markets. In keeping with President Trump’s pledge to eliminate cartels, OFAC has prioritized targeting these and other criminal groups that threaten the welfare of Americans. Treasury has coordinated closely with the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF), taking nearly 40 actions against over 500 individuals and entities since the beginning of 2025.  OFAC uses a network-based approach to simultaneously disrupt as many different facets of the cartels as possible, from their leadership and key organizational nodes to facilitators and enablers, such as corrupt officials, complicit family members, and ostensibly legitimate front persons. Today’s action reflects a unified, whole-of-government effort to ensure operational coordination and maximize impact against transnational criminal networks.  OFAC conducted its investigation in parallel with the HSTF, with support from the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Drug Enforcement Administration, and Homeland Security Investigations.  OFAC continues to work closely with the HSTF to disrupt the flow of illicit drugs and dismantle the networks, facilitators, and financial infrastructure that enable their production and distribution. Additionally, OFAC worked closely with valued international partners, including the Australian Federal Police, New Zealand Police, Italy’s Guardia di Finanza, and Canada’s Royal Canadian Mounted Police and York Regional Police, whose cooperation was instrumental in supporting today’s action. The action was taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 14059, which targets the proliferation of illicit drugs and their means of production. COMANCHERO OUTLAW MOTORCYCLE GANG Today, OFAC designated the Comancheros , also known as the Comanchero Motorcycle Club or simply Comanchero MC , an Australian drug trafficking organization with an international footprint in Asia, Europe, and North America.  Developing strategic partnerships with U.S. sanctioned cartels, including the Sinaloa Cartel, CJNG, Clan del Golfo, and Los Choneros, the Comancheros have facilitated multi-hundred-kilogram shipments of cocaine from South America to the United States, Australia, and Europe.  The Comancheros have also been involved in other criminal activity around the world, including assassinations, arms trafficking, and money laundering. Because Australia and New Zealand are some of the world’s most lucrative illicit drug markets, Mexican cartels are increasingly targeting these markets to capitalize on the significantly higher margins and growing demand.  Due to the geographic distance from the major cocaine producing regions in the Western Hemisphere, cartels can charge substantial premiums compared to drugs sold in the United States.  The Sinaloa Cartel has been known to send “sleeper cells” to Australia to facilitate local drug distribution and establish contacts with the Comancheros and other outlaw motorcycle gangs who assist with the logistics of drug trafficking. The Comancheros are being designated under E.O. 14059 for having engaged in, or having attempted to engage in, activities or transactions that have materially contributed to, or pose a significant risk of materially contributing to, the international proliferation of illicit drugs or their means of production. COMANCHERO COMMAND AND CONTROL Alexandre Varela Villar , better known as Alex Vare ( Vare ), is the Spain-based World Commander of the Comancheros. Allan John Norman Meehan , better known as Allan Meehan ( Meehan ), is the Australia-based World President of the Comancheros. Pasilika Naufahu ( Pasilika ) is the national president of the New Zealand chapter of the Comancheros.  Before being deported to New Zealand in 2016, Pasilika was the sergeant-at-arms of the Comancheros in Australia.  Pasilika was arrested and sentenced to 10 years in prison in February 2021 for various charges related to his position in the Comancheros.  In close coordination with his brother and senior Comancheros member, Vetekina Naufahu ( Vetekina ), Pasilika has facilitated multi-hundred-kilogram importations of drugs into New Zealand and has established connections to the Sinaloa Cartel. Marco Francis Coffen ( Coffen ) is an associate of the Comancheros and has been involved in supplying multiple Australian criminal organizations, including the Comancheros, with encrypted communication platforms to drug traffickers and shielding them from police phone taps. Vare and Meehan are being designated pursuant to E.O. 14059 for being or having been leaders or officials of the Comancheros. Pasilika and Vetekina are being designated pursuant to E.O. 14059 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, the Comancheros. Coffen is being designated pursuant to E.O. 14059 for having provided, or attempted to provide, financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services in support of, the Comancheros. OMERTÀ – THE ‘NDRANGHETA The ‘Ndrangheta , an international drug trafficking organization and mafia-type criminal syndicate, operates in over 80 countries and continues to grow.  The ‘Ndrangheta’s adherence to omertà , a code of silence, and its reliance on deeply rooted familial bloodlines have enabled the organization to maintain secrecy, foster loyalty, resist infiltration, and expand its criminal influence across generations and international borders.  While the ‘Ndrangheta was founded in Calabria, Italy, the organization has expanded across Europe, the Western Hemisphere, and Australia.  As one of the largest criminal organizations in the world, the ‘Ndrangheta’s primary business comes from drug trafficking, with some estimates stating that almost 80 percent of the European cocaine trade is controlled by the ‘Ndrangheta.  While primarily focused on the cocaine trade, Italian officials have stated that the ‘Ndrangheta have started expanding into the illicit fentanyl market. The ’Ndrangheta frequently partner with Mexican and South American drug trafficking organizations and FTOs, including the Sinaloa Cartel, CJNG, and Clan del Golfo.  In the past, the ‘Ndrangheta has also partnered with other Mexican drug trafficking organizations and FTOs, including Los Zetas (now known as Cartel del Noreste) and the Gulf Cartel. The ‘Ndrangheta was previously designated on May 30, 2008 , pursuant to the Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Designation Act (Kingpin Act).  Today, the ‘Ndrangheta is being designated pursuant to E.O. 14059 for having engaged in, or having attempted to engage in, activities or transactions that have materially contributed to, or pose a significant risk of materially contributing to, the international proliferation of illicit drugs or their means of production. ‘NDRANGHETISTI NORTH OF THE BORDER Locali (singular: locale ) are the primary territorial organizational unit of the ‘Ndrangheta, comprising members known as ‘ ndranghetisti , that oversee and coordinate criminal activities within a specific geographical region.  The ‘Ndrangheta locale that operates in the Greater Toronto Area in Canada has strengthened in recent years, becoming so powerful that they dictate events in Italy from across the ocean.  In Canada, the ‘Ndrangheta is involved in drug trafficking, money laundering, murder, and other crimes.  This faction of the ‘Ndrangheta uses the U.S. and Canadian financial systems to launder illicit proceeds. Today, OFAC designated Italian-born Angelo Figliomeni (also known as “Don Angelino”), the leader of the Toronto faction of the ‘Ndrangheta.  A member of the Figliomeni ‘ndrina (family), Angelo Figliomeni fled to Canada in the early 2000’s to escape a 20-year sentence for weapons charges in Italy.  Angelo’s power extends beyond Canada, stretching back to Italy.  He has engaged in money laundering and other criminal activities on behalf of the ‘Ndrangheta. Another member of the Figliomeni ‘ndrina is Italian-born Cosimo Figliomeni (sometimes known as “Cosimino”), who is a top leader of the ‘Ndrangheta faction in Toronto and has been the subject of criminal proceedings in Italy in connection to his role within the ‘Ndrangheta organization. OFAC also designated two members of the Commisso ‘ndrina who are long time Italian-born leaders of the ‘Ndrangheta in Toronto. Francesco Commisso , also known as “U Scelto,” has faced allegations in Italy of being part of a Toronto oversight body that was tasked, among other duties, with imposing disciplinary sanctions on members. Rocco Remo Commisso (also known as Remo Commisso ) is a Canada-based leader of the ‘Ndrangheta and leads narcotics trafficking networks within the United States, including in the state of New York.  Remo Commisso was convicted in Canada in 1981 for conspiracy to commit murder and again in 1984 for his involvement in a bombing that killed one person.  Remo Commisso is involved in narcotics trafficking in the United States for the ‘Ndrangheta, including in New York. Vincenzo DeMaria (also known as Jimmy DeMaria ) is one of Toronto’s top ‘Ndrangheta bosses and has been active in the Toronto organized crime scene for decades.  DeMaria shot and killed a man in 1981 over a $2,000 drug debt and was convicted of second-degree murder in 1982.  He has since been released from prison and holds significant power in the ‘Ndrangheta. Cosimo Figliomeni, Francesco Commisso, Remo Commisso, and Jimmy DeMaria make up the Camera di Controllo of Toronto, a collegial body of the ‘Ndrangheta that decides on important questions concerning the organization and settles disputes, even outside of Toronto.  The Toronto ‘Ndrangheta is tightly connected throughout the world and has close relationships with members back in Calabria. Luigi Vescio Sr. (also known as “The Undertaker” or “Lui Vescio”) is a Canadian-born ‘Ndrangheta senior member and associate of Angelo Figliomeni and Jimmy DeMaria. Angelo Figliomeni, Cosimo Figliomeni, Francesco Commisso, Remo Commisso, and Luigi Vescio Sr. were all charged in the Italian Court of Reggio Calabria for mafia-type association related to their leadership, membership, and promotion of the ‘Ndrangheta in 2019. Angelo Figliomeni, Cosimo Figliomeni, Francesco Commisso, Remo Commisso, Jimmy DeMaria, and Luigi Vescio Sr. are being designated pursuant to E.O. 14059 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, ‘Ndrangheta. FAMILY-OWNED, MAFIA-CONNECTED – VESCIO FUNERAL HOMES OFAC is also designating the corporate network of Vescio Sr., including his network of funeral homes in Ontario.  These funeral homes include the Fratelli Vescio Funeral Homes Ltd. in Woodbridge, Ontario, Vescio Funeral Homes Ltd. in Toronto and Vescio Funeral Home (Maple) Inc. in Maple, Ontario.  Vescio Sr. also controls a Toronto-based luxury limousine rental business, Phantom Limousine Services Inc. Vescio Sr. serves as the president of each of these companies. OFAC is also designating Luigi Vescio Sr.’s wife, Rose Vescio , and his two children, Luigi Vescio Jr. and Laura Vescio , for their roles in owning and operating the Vescio Funeral Homes on behalf of Luigi Vescio Sr. Rose Vescio, Luigi Vescio Jr., and Laura Vescio are being designated pursuant to E.O. 14059 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Luigi Vescio Sr. SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of blocked persons. Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis. OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities involving designated or otherwise blocked persons.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person. The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List), but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law.  The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior.  For information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on Filing a Petition for Removal from an OFAC List . To view the chart on the Comancheros network designated today, click here . To view the chart on the ‘Ndrangheta network designated today, click here . Click here for more information on the persons designated today . ###

title: Treasury Targets Cyber Scam Operators and Armed Group Facilitators in Southeast Asia
body: November 19, 2026 WASHINGTON —Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned three individuals involved in operating and facilitating cyber scam centers in Southeast Asia, as well as two affiliated companies.  The individuals designated today include operators of scam compounds that target Americans through virtual currency investment fraud and affiliates of armed groups that provide protection and support to scam-center networks in Southeast Asia. “Under President Trump’s leadership, Treasury has aggressively targeted overseas scam compounds to protect Americans from fraud,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent .  “We will continue to use all available tools to disrupt and dismantle the networks that enable scam compounds to operate.” These actions are being taken in furtherance of President Trump’s Executive Order (E.O.) 14390 of March 6, 2026, “Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens,” which orders the U.S. Government to unleash every available tool to stop foreign-backed criminal networks that exploit vulnerable Americans through cybercrime, cyber-enabled fraud, and extortion.  Today’s action further reflects OFAC’s coordination with the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s New York Field Office, Department of Justice’s Scam Center Strike Force, and the Drug Enforcement Administration, and the Homeland Security Task Force and National Coordination Center.  OFAC is taking today’s actions pursuant to E.O. 13694, as amended by E.O. 13757, E.O. 14144, and E.O. 14306 (“E.O. 13694, as further amended”). ZHAO HUI: A SCAM CENTER OPERATOR Zhao Hui (Zhao) is a Cambodian national who leased a scam center owned by the OFAC-designated Prince Group TCO and paid protection fees to the OFAC-designated leader of the Prince Group TCO, Chen Zhi .  In addition, Zhao owned a scam compound in Cambodia independent of Prince Group TCO.  At this scam compound, Zhao was directly involved in scam operations and managed this scam compound’s leases.  This scam compound primarily targeted Americans and Europeans.  Such scam compounds conduct virtual currency investment scams.  Since Zhao has leased a scam compound and owned and operated an additional scam compound in Cambodia, he has materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of virtual cryptocurrency investment scams, an activity described in subsection 1(a)(ii) of E.O. 13694, as further amended. Zhao is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, an activity described in subsection 1(a)(ii) of E.O. 13694, as further amended. Zhao is the chairman of the board of directors of Cambodia-based construction company Bei Fang Bo Lin Construction Decoration Co., Ltd . (Bei Fang Bo Lin) and management and consultancy company ZHZ Investment Consulting Co., Ltd. (ZHZ Investment). Bei Fang Bo Lin and ZHZ Investment are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended, for being owned or controlled by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Zhao Hui. THE DKBA’S FACILITATION OF SCAM COMPOUND ACTIVITY In recent years, armed groups in Burma have transformed a strip along the Thai-Burmese border into one of the world’s highest concentrations of scam centers.  The Democratic Karen Benevolent Army (DKBA) is an ethnic armed group previously designated by OFAC for supporting cyber scam centers in Burma that target Americans using fraudulent investment schemes.  DKBA actors not only provide security for scam compounds and permit their continued operation, but also actively participate in violence against victims of human trafficking trapped inside the compounds. Since December 2025, General Saw Shwe Wah has been the commander-in-chief of the DKBA, replacing General Saw Steel , who OFAC designated in November 2025 pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended. Colonel Saw A One is the DKBA commander who oversees security in the Three Pagodas Pass in Karen State near the Thai border.  The region has seen expansion of new buildings intended for telecom scam operations, with many scam actors entering the area with the assistance of the DKBA, which also protects them.  Saw A One reportedly owns a plantation where scam operations occur and has contracted for scam operations. Saw Shwe Wah and Saw A One are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended, for being or having been leaders, officials, senior executive officers, or members of the board of directors of the DKBA, a person whose property and interests in property are blocked pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended. SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S.  persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons. Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis.  OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities involving designated or otherwise blocked persons.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions.  Individuals located in the U.S. or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to FinCEN’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000. The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the SDN List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List, when consistent with relevant statutes and other authorities.   The ultimate goal of sanctions is to bring about a positive change in behavior.  What constitutes a sufficient change in circumstance will vary based on context, including the status of the broader geopolitical circumstances affecting the national security and foreign policy interests implicated by the declared national emergency. For more information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on How to Request Removal from an OFAC List . title: Treasury’s Office of Cybersecurity and Critical Infrastructure Protection Issues Annual Consumer Advisory on Holiday Scams
body: November 18, 2026 WASHINGTON – Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Cybersecurity and Critical Infrastructure Protection (OCCIP) released its annual holiday advisory to help consumers protect themselves from the seasonal surge in cyber-enabled scams and online fraud. As frauds and scams continue to proliferate, including through the use of super intelligence, it is important to remember that anyone can be a victim of fraud. Learn how to identify fraudulent activity, disrupt scammers, and report incidents quickly to keep yourself and others safe. This holiday season, Treasury urges consumers to stay vigilant, be proactive, and respond quickly if they believe they are being targeted. Share your stories and experiences with your community to help teach others how to stay safe from scams. "As cybercriminals increasingly leverage super intelligence (SI) to carry out more sophisticated and convincing scams, it is more important than ever for Americans to remain vigilant this holiday season." said Cory Wilson, Deputy Assistant Secretary for Cybersecurity and Critical Infrastructure Protection.  "Cybercriminals are exploiting SI to impersonate trusted individuals, businesses, and even loved ones, putting Americans and their hard-earned money at risk.  Treasury remains committed to strengthening consumer resilience against cyber-enabled fraud through education, awareness, and actionable guidance. We encourage all Americans to take a moment to verify suspicious requests, recognize the warning signs of fraud, and report all suspected scams to the appropriate authorities." Access OCCIP’s Staying Cyber-Safe this Holiday Season . Report fraud to the Federal Trade Commission at ReportFraud.ftc.gov and the Federal Bureau of Investigation Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) . ###

title: Treasury International Capital Data for September
body: November 18, 2026 WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of the Treasury today released Treasury International Capital (TIC) data for September 2026.  The next release, which will report on data for October 2026, is scheduled for December 15, 2026. The sum total in September of all net foreign acquisitions of long-term securities, short-term U.S. securities, and banking flows was a net TIC inflow of $261.0 billion.  Of this, net foreign private inflows were $267.0 billion, and net foreign official outflows were $6.0 billion. Foreign residents increased their holdings of long-term U.S. securities in September; their net purchases were $186.7 billion.  Net purchases by private foreign investors were $148.3 billion, and net purchases by foreign official institutions were $38.4 billion. U.S. residents increased their holdings of long-term foreign securities, with net purchases of $31.4 billion. After including adjustments, such as estimated foreign portfolio acquisitions of U.S. stocks through stock swaps, overall net foreign purchases of long-term securities are estimated to have been $155.3 billion in September. Foreign residents increased their holdings of U.S. Treasury bills by $3.5 billion.  Foreign resident holdings of all dollar-denominated short-term U.S. securities and other custody liabilities decreased by $2.9 billion. Banks’ own net dollar-denominated liabilities to foreign residents increased by $108.6 billion. Complete data are available on the Treasury website here . ### About TIC Data The monthly data on holdings of long-term securities, as well as the monthly table on Major Foreign Holders of Treasury Securities, reflect foreign holdings of U.S. securities collected primarily on the basis of custodial data.  These data help provide a window into foreign ownership of U.S. securities, but they cannot attribute holdings of U.S. securities with complete accuracy.  For example, if a U.S. Treasury security purchased by a foreign resident is held in a custodial account in a third country, the true ownership of the security will not be reflected in the data.  The custodial data will also not properly attribute U.S. Treasury securities managed by foreign private portfolio managers who invest on behalf of residents of other countries.  In addition, foreign countries may hold dollars and other U.S. assets that are not captured in the TIC data.  For these reasons, it is difficult to draw precise conclusions from TIC data about changes in the foreign holdings of U.S. financial assets by individual countries. title: Operation Economic Outcast Targets Iran’s Proxy Networks
body: November 18, 2026 Targets Include Hizballah-Affiliated Charity, Gold and Cash Smuggling Network WASHINGTON —Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated the Wa Ta’awanu Association (Wa Ta’awanu), a Hizballah-affiliated charity that provides cover for Hizballah’s activities under the guise of delivering humanitarian services. OFAC today also designated members of a Lebanon- and Türkiye-based gold and cash smuggling network run by Hizballah and Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force (IRGC-QF). “The Iranian regime’s attempts to infringe on Lebanon’s sovereignty through terror proxies like Hizballah will not be tolerated,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent .  “The U.S. government will continue to disrupt Iran’s attempts to exert influence in the region and fund its proxies.” Today’s action exposes Hizballah’s continued exploitation of civilian charitable organizations and its efforts to portray itself as a provider of humanitarian assistance.  It also increases pressure on the group’s illicit financing networks as Hizballah seeks to resist growing calls and international pressure to disarm. Today’s action is being taken pursuant to the United States’ counterterrorism authority, Executive Order (E.O.) 13224, as amended.  The U.S. Department of State designated Hizballah as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist pursuant to E.O. 13224 on October 31, 2001, for having committed, or posing a significant risk of committing, acts of terrorism that threaten the security of U.S. nationals or the national security, foreign policy, or economy of the United States.  Previously, the U.S. Department of State had designated Hizballah as a Foreign Terrorist Organization (FTO) pursuant to section 219 of the Immigration and Nationality Act on October 8, 1997.  OFAC also designated Hizballah pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, on August 20, 2026 for being owned, controlled, or directed by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, the IRGC-QF. HIZBALLAH’S ABUSE OF THE CHARITABLE SECTOR Hizballah-affiliated Wa Ta’awanu is a Lebanon-based charity that provides emergency relief services for southern Lebanon while also channeling outside donor funds toward Hizballah’s terrorist activities.  In July 2026, as part of the June 26, 2026 Trilateral Framework between the United States, Lebanon, and Israel, the Lebanese Armed Forces moved into areas previously held by the Israeli military to secure those areas and ensure that they were free from Hizballah fighters and weapons.  However, Wa Ta’awanu provides a pretext for Hizballah’s militant activities in the pilot zones, preventing disarmament and inhibiting Lebanese government efforts to safeguard these areas.  Wa Ta’awanu founder Afif Abdel Rida Chouman leads the charity and coordinates the organization’s activities at Hizballah’s direction. Wa Ta’awanu and Afif Abdel Rida Chouman are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Hizballah. HIZBALLAH GOLD AND CASH NETWORK In coordination with Hizballah financial officials, Lebanese businessman and money changer Hassan Khechen and his brother Ibrahim Khechen have transferred significant funds over the course of their operations from the IRGC-QF to Lebanon on behalf of Hizballah.  Hassan Khechen is the owner of Lebanon-based Gold Global Company , which he uses to transfer money from several transit countries to Lebanon for Hizballah.  Hassan Khechen’s network also employs couriers to transfer funds in cash across borders.  Hassan Khechen’s brother, Ibrahim Khechen, also participates in Hizballah’s money smuggling network and has links to a related courier who was arrested in February 2025 at the Beirut airport with $2.5 million in his hand luggage.  Türkiye-based and Hizballah-affiliated Sankari Gold Kuyumculuk Ticaret Limited Sirketi (Sankari Gold), also controlled by Hassan Khechen, assists Gold Global Company in moving gold bullion and cash from Africa. Hassan Khechen and Ibrahim Khechen are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Hizballah.  Gold Global Company and Sankari Gold is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for being owned, controlled, or directed by, or for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Hassan Khechen. SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons. Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis. OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities involving designated or otherwise blocked persons.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions.  Individuals located in the United States or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000. Furthermore, engaging in certain transactions involving the persons designated today may risk the imposition of secondary sanctions on participating foreign financial institutions.  OFAC can prohibit or impose strict conditions on opening or maintaining, in the United States, a correspondent account or a payable-through account of a foreign financial institution that knowingly conducts or facilitates any significant transaction on behalf of a person who is designated pursuant to the relevant authority. The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the SDN List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List, when consistent with relevant statutes and other authorities.   A goal of sanctions is to bring about a positive change in behavior.  What constitutes a sufficient change in circumstance will vary based on context, including the status of the broader geopolitical circumstances affecting the national security and foreign policy interests implicated by the declared national emergency.  OFAC sanctions determinations, including removal determinations, are made consistent with Administration foreign policy and national security policies and priorities.  For more information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on How to Request Removal from an OFAC List. Click here for more information on today’s designations . ###

title: November 18, 2026 - FDA Approves First Drug to Treat Neurological Symptoms of Type 3 Gaucher Disease
body: FDA News Release FDA Approves First Drug to Treat Neurological Symptoms of Type 3 Gaucher Disease For Immediate Release: November 18, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved Infilbray (venglustat) tablets, the first treatment for the neurological symptoms of Type 3 Gaucher disease (GD3) in adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 15 kg (approximately 33 pounds). Infilbray crosses the blood-brain barrier to reduce the accumulation of harmful substances in the body and brain. “For patients with Type 3 Gaucher disease, harmful substances build up in the brain without a way to stop them, but this drug's ability to cross the blood-brain barrier means it can get to the source of the buildup driving the neurological symptoms,” said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas, J.D. “This approval reflects the FDA’s commitment to advancing therapeutic options for patients with rare diseases and brings an important new treatment to patients and the healthcare providers who care for them.” GD3 is a rare, inherited condition in which the body cannot properly break down fatty substances, called glucosphingolipids, due to a deficient or malfunctioning enzyme. As these substances accumulate in organs, tissues, and the brain, patients experience a wide range of serious health problems over time. Unlike type 1 Gaucher disease, GD3 also affects the brain and nervous system, causing difficulties with balance, coordination, speech, memory, and thinking — symptoms that can worsen progressively and significantly impact quality of life. Infilbray works as a glucosylceramide synthase inhibitor, reducing the buildup of harmful substances throughout the body and, critically, within the brain. The FDA’s approval of Infilbray is supported by data from a randomized, double-blind, multicenter clinical study enrolling 43 patients aged 12 years and older with GD3 who had previously been treated with enzyme replacement therapy and had achieved systemic disease stabilization. Participants received either Infilbray orally once daily or intravenous enzyme replacement therapy every two weeks for 52 weeks. Treatment effectiveness was evaluated using two assessments that capture the neurological symptoms central to daily life in patients with GD3, including those related to ataxia (loss of muscle control and coordination) and cognitive function. At Week 52, patients treated with Infilbray demonstrated improvement on a measure that combined both assessments compared to those taking enzyme replacement therapy for the treatment of non-neurologic manifestations of GD3. The most frequently reported side effects of Infilbray include gastrointestinal symptoms as well as adverse effects on mood. Serious psychiatric risks, including suicidal ideation and behavior, have been reported. Potential risks identified from animal studies include potential clouding of vision in younger patients and adverse effects on fetal development when drug is taken during pregnancy. More information on side effects can be found in the drug labeling. Infilbray was granted Orphan Drug designation as well as Priority Review . The approval of Infilbray was granted to Genzyme Corporation, a Sanofi Company. title: FinCEN Issues Proposed Rule to Strengthen Customer Due Diligence Requirements for Covered Financial Institutions
body: November 17, 2026 WASHINGTON —Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) issued a proposed rule to strengthen customer due diligence requirements, which are integral to efforts to combat money laundering and counter the financing of terrorism. FinCEN issues this proposal as a part of Treasury’s implementation of Executive Order 14406, Restoring Integrity to America’s Financial System . “Financial institutions are on the front lines of protecting our financial systems from criminal organizations and cartels that target law-abiding businesses and workers,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent . “This proposed rule cuts unnecessary burden, gives institutions more flexibility to effectively combat risk, and strengthens our fight against financial crime.” The proposed rule would amend customer due diligence requirements to: explicitly provide that covered financial institutions can obtain additional information about beneficial owners of a legal entity customer that may be useful in mitigating risk or addressing supervisory concerns; codify exceptive relief FinCEN issued removing the requirement for covered financial institutions to identify and verify the beneficial owners of a legal entity customer each time the customer opens a new account; and specify information that a covered financial institution must obtain about each beneficial owner of a legal entity customer. FinCEN welcomes public comments. The comment period closes 60 days after the proposed rule’s publication in the Federal Register . Resources Notice of Proposed Rulemaking Fact Sheet ###

title: Treasury, IRS Issue Final Rules to Help Hardworking Americans Build a Financially Secure Retirement
body: November 17, 2026 SECURE 2.0 Final Regulations Expand Automatic Enrollment in Workplace Retirement Plans WASHINGTON — The U.S. Department of the Treasury and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) today issued final regulations to help more Americans save for retirement through their workplaces. The regulations implement a key provision of the SECURE 2.0 Act, providing employers with clear guidance on automatic enrollment for certain 401(k) and 403(b) retirement plans. The rules help workers build retirement savings while preserving their control over how much they contribute. Treasury estimates that SECURE 2.0’s automatic enrollment expansion provision will increase retirement savings by an average of $4.2 billion annually over the 2023-2032 period. “A financially secure retirement is a cornerstone of the American Dream, and every worker deserves the opportunity to achieve it,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent . “Today’s rules help more American families and workers build retirement savings while keeping them in control of their contributions, and give employers the clarity and flexibility to invest in their employees’ futures.” “With the SECURE 2.0 regulations in place, American families will be able to boost their savings and keep more of their hard-earned money through their automatic enrollment in a retirement account,” said IRS Chief Executive Officer Frank J. Bisignano . “These regulations reduce the administrative burden placed on taxpayers when making long-term financial decisions. More broadly, they further the IRS goal of improving taxpayer service by making interactions with the Service simpler and easier.” STRENGTHENING AMERICANS’ RETIREMENT SAVINGS The final regulations implement a key provision of the SECURE 2.0 Act by clarifying requirements for plan sponsors and simplifying certain participant notices. Covered retirement plans generally must automatically enroll eligible employees at a contribution rate of three percent. After an initial participation period, the default contribution rate must generally increase by at least one percentage point each year until it reaches at least ten percent, subject to a fifteen percent maximum. Employees may opt out or choose a different contribution rate. The final regulations generally apply to retirement plan years beginning after December 31, 2027, giving employers time to make necessary administrative changes. The final regulations: Clarify statutory exceptions for qualifying small and new businesses, governmental plans, church plans, and SIMPLE 401(k) plans; Give employers flexibility in the timing and amount of automatic contribution increases, within statutory limits; Simplify plan communications by allowing certain required notices to be combined and reducing annual notice requirements for qualifying employees who are not participating, provided they receive annual reminders and any plan documents they are entitled to request; and Explain how automatic enrollment requirements apply following plan mergers. The final regulations are available here . ###

title: November 17, 2026 - FDA Launches the Global Reliance Disclosure Program to Expand Patient Access to Medicines Worldwide
body: FDA News Release FDA Launches the Global Reliance Disclosure Program to Expand Patient Access to Medicines Worldwide For Immediate Release: November 17, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today announced the Global Reliance Disclosure Program (GRDP), a landmark initiative that will fundamentally transform how the FDA's regulatory drug and biologic approval decisions are leveraged by health authorities around the world. The GRDP marks a major step forward in the FDA's global leadership and may accelerate patient access to innovative therapies throughout the world. The GRDP enables the FDA to more efficiently share minimally redacted approval packages, including the FDA's detailed scientific and regulatory assessments, directly with companies who can then share them with regulatory authorities outside of the United States, empowering those authorities to rely on the FDA's rigorous, science-based review decisions rather than conducting duplicative and time-consuming product evaluations of their own, while maintaining sovereignty over their regulatory decision. "The GRDP is a prime example of America First policies improving public health worldwide," said Grace Graham, FDA Deputy Commissioner for Policy, Legislation, and International Affairs . "The FDA is the global gold standard and making it easier for applicants to leverage our detailed scientific assessments to facilitate faster access for patients everywhere is an example of America’s continued interest in advancing global health under the Trump Administration." The GRDP launched on Oct. 30, with a President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) tentative approval for lenacapavir , a drug indicated for both HIV prevention and treatment. This is an especially meaningful starting point given PEPFAR's life-saving mission to combat HIV/AIDS in some of the world's most vulnerable populations. The GRDP is currently available to PEPFAR tentative approvals, excluding tentatively approved abbreviated new drug application products. However, the FDA intends to expand the GRDP in January 2027 to all novel drug and biologics (New Molecular Entity New Drug Applications and 351(a) Biologics License Applications), dramatically broadening the program's reach and impact. The FDA also intends to launch a pathway in early 2027 to expedite an applicant’s ability to request their minimally redacted action packages for approved and licensed drugs and biologics, accelerating global access to medicines that are already on the market in the United States and have been found to be safe and effective by the FDA. To receive a minimally redacted application approval package as part of the GRDP, applicants must request to participate within 10 calendar days of approval and confirm the application package is being submitted to a foreign regulatory authority in support of a marketing application. Applicants with eligible GRDP applications will receive detailed information in FDA approval letters and the agency intends to provide the minimally redacted package on an expedited basis. Requests for minimally redacted approval packages for other purposes will not be processed under the GRDP and should be submitted as a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request. “In an era of increasing global interdependence in pharmaceutical development and supply chains, the FDA's leadership is most effective when it is collaborative,” said Mark Abdoo, FDA Associate Commissioner for Global Policy and Strategy . “The GRDP reflects a forward-looking vision of regulatory leadership: one defined not by exclusivity, but by the willingness to share expertise, elevate global standards, and put patients first — wherever they are.” The GRDP addresses one of the most persistent and consequential challenges in global health: the gap between regulatory approval in high-capacity countries and patient access in lower-resource settings. When a drug is approved by the FDA, patients in many parts of the world may wait months or years longer for their own national health authority to complete an independent review due to limited regulatory capacity and resources. Beyond individual product approvals, the GRDP supports global health security. Harmonized regulatory decisions reduce the risk of fragmented or inconsistent product standards across markets, helping to ensure that the same high-quality therapies reach patients regardless of where they live, including here in the United States.
