title: November 17, 2026 - FDA Approves First Drug Shown to Help Patients with Infantile-Onset Niemann-Pick Disease Type C Live Longer
body: FDA News Release FDA Approves First Drug Shown to Help Patients with Infantile-Onset Niemann-Pick Disease Type C Live Longer New therapy offers a meaningful treatment option for families facing a rare and serious childhood disease For Immediate Release: November 17, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved Lembaz (adrabetadex) injection, the first treatment shown to help people with a severe form of Niemann-Pick disease type C (NPC) live longer. Lembaz is approved to reduce the risk of death in adult and pediatric patients who weigh at least 7 kg (about 15 pounds) and whose neurological symptoms began before age 6, also known as infantile-onset NPC. “For families living with Niemann-Pick disease type C, today’s approval marks an important milestone,” said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas, J.D. “For the first time, there is a treatment shown to help adults and children with this serious disease live longer, and we are committed to continuing to support the development of therapies for the rare disease community.” Niemann-Pick disease type C (NPC) is a rare, inherited lysosomal storage disorder affecting an estimated 1 in 150,000 people, in which the body cannot properly process cholesterol and other fats inside cells. Over time, these substances accumulate — particularly in the brain — causing progressive neurological decline, including loss of movement, coordination, and the ability to swallow. Patients whose neurological symptoms begin before age 6 face the most serious form of the disease. Prior to this approval action, two therapies were approved for NPC, but neither has been shown to reduce the risk of death. Both carry age and weight restrictions that limit access for the youngest and most seriously affected patients. Lembaz is the first FDA-approved therapy to reduce the risk of death in adults and children weighing at least 7 kg (about 15 pounds) with NPC whose neurological symptoms began before age 6. A trained healthcare provider gives Lembaz as an injection directly into the spinal canal — a procedure called an intrathecal injection — every two weeks. To assess whether Lembaz reduced the risk of death, the FDA examined the survival of 36 patients treated with Lembaz across three clinical studies and an expanded access program. All patients had neurological manifestations of NPC that occurred prior to age 6. Patients treated with Lembaz had longer overall survival compared to the matched external control group, with a 55% reduction in the risk of death. The median survival time was 8.5 years for the treated group compared with 4.9 years in the control group. This survival benefit was observed regardless of whether patients were also taking miglustat, a therapy used off-label in NPC. The most common side effects of Lembaz include problems with hearing, balance and coordination, fatigue, vomiting, back pain, headache, fever, diarrhea, nausea, and cough. Lembaz carries a boxed warning for hearing impairment, including permanent hearing loss. A comprehensive hearing evaluation should be performed on patients before starting Lembaz and regularly throughout treatment, and dose adjustments may be needed based on the results of these evaluations. Lembaz received Breakthrough Therapy designation. The FDA granted approval of Lembaz to Mandos, LLC, a subsidiary of Beren Therapeutics, PBC. title: Treasury Sanctions Guatemalan Drug Trafficking Organizations Supporting Mexican Narco-Terrorist Cartels
body: November 13, 2026 WASHINGTON — Today, the Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned the Los Mendoza Drug Trafficking Organization (DTO) and the Los Huistas DTO for supporting Mexico’s largest narco-terrorist groups, the Sinaloa Cartel and Cartel de Jalisco Nueva Generacion (CJNG), which the Trump Administration has designated as both Foreign Terrorist Organizations (FTOs) and Specially Designated Global Terrorists (SDGTs) last year.  Based in Guatemala, Los Mendoza DTO and Los Huistas DTO control strategic trafficking corridors along the borders with Honduras and Mexico, making them indispensable logistics partners for the Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG. “Today’s action exposes the ties between politically influential Guatemalan criminal organizations and Mexican foreign terrorist organizations that facilitate the flow of deadly narcotics into the United States,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent .  “Under President Trump’s America First agenda, the Treasury Department will continue to target the criminal networks that enable violent organizations like the Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG to traffic drugs across our borders and threaten the safety of the American people.” The Los Mendoza DTO and Los Huistas DTO facilitate the receipt, storage, protection, and cross-border movement of narcotics destined for the United States and other international markets.  Through longstanding alliances spanning Central and South America, the Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG have expanded their criminal operations, established sophisticated cross-border trafficking networks, and consolidated control over critical segments of the illicit drug supply chain.  By targeting these key facilitators, OFAC is disrupting critical nodes in the supply chains that enable the trafficking of fentanyl, cocaine, methamphetamine, and other illicit drugs throughout the region. The action was taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 14059, which targets the international proliferation of illicit drugs and their means of production, and pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended by E.O. 13886 (collectively, “E.O.13224, as amended”), which targets terrorists and their supporters. This action was done in coordination with the Department of State who is taking action against narcoterrorists destabilizing the Western Hemisphere.  In a concurrent action, the Department of State is also designating Los Lorenzanas as both an FTO pursuant to section 219 of the Immigration and Nationality Act, and as an SDGT pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended. SINALOA CARTEL AND CJNG: LEVERAGING GUATEMALAN ALLIANCES TO FACILITATE DRUG TRAFFICKING Today, OFAC is sanctioning Los Mendoza DTO pursuant to E.O. 14059 and pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for providing material support to the Sinaloa Cartel.  Additionally, OFAC is sanctioning Los Huistas DTO pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for providing material support to the Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG.  In Guatemala, Los Mendoza DTO and Los Huistas DTO play important roles in facilitating narco-trafficking activities by controlling strategic trafficking corridors along the country’s borders with Honduras and Mexico.  The Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG collaborate with local criminal groups like Los Mendoza DTO and Los Huistas DTO to manage key logistical operations, including the receipt, storage, and cross-border transportation of narcotics, in order to move narcotics into Mexico for distribution in the United States and other international markets. The Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG are the most powerful cartels in Mexico and responsible for a significant portion of deadly drugs trafficked into the United States.  In addition to trafficking fentanyl, methamphetamine, cocaine, and other illicit drugs into the United States, these cartels have engaged in widespread violence and other criminal endeavors, such as fuel theft and timeshare fraud.  On February 20, 2025 , the Department of State designated both the Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG as FTOs and SDGTs.  The Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG were each also identified by the United States as significant foreign narcotics traffickers on April 15, 2009 and on April 8, 2015 , respectively, pursuant to the Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Designation Act. On December 15, 2021 , OFAC also designated the Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG pursuant to E.O. 14059. LOS MENDOZA AND LOS HUISTAS DTOS – KEY LOGISTICS PARTNERS Founded in the 1980s, Los Mendoza DTO is one of Guatemala’s oldest and most powerful criminal organizations.  The family-based organization operates as a key transportation and logistics intermediary for the Sinaloa Cartel, facilitating drug trafficking operations across Guatemala and Honduras.  Los Mendoza DTO supports the Sinaloa Cartel’s trafficking network by facilitating access to border crossings, clandestine airstrips, storage facilities, and local protection networks in the Guatemalan departments of San Marcos, Huehuetenango, and Peten.  Beyond narcotics trafficking, Los Mendoza DTO is involved in contract killings and money laundering, and has amassed significant economic interests through land dispossession, cattle ranching, agricultural businesses, and real estate investments across Peten, Izabal, and Guatemala’s border region with Mexico. Active since the 1990s, Los Huistas DTO is one of Guatemala’s most powerful and longstanding criminal organizations.  Los Huistas DTO serves as a critical link in the cocaine trafficking supply chain from South America through Mexico and ultimately into the United States.  On March 18, 2022, OFAC designated Los Huistas DTO pursuant to E.O. 14059.  Los Huistas DTO maintains operational ties with both the Sinaloa Cartel and CJNG, providing logistical support and protection for narcotics shipments.  Los Huistas DTO’s longstanding ties to local businessmen, law enforcement officials, and politicians have enabled it to dominate the underworld in parts of northwestern Guatemala.  Through these relationships, Los Huistas DTO has cultivated political influence and institutional access which have facilitated its criminal operations and helped to shield the organization from the purview of law enforcement. SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons. Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis. OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities involving designated or otherwise blocked persons.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions.  Individuals located in the United States or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network’s (FinCEN’s) whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000. Furthermore, engaging in certain transactions involving the persons designated today may risk the imposition of secondary sanctions on participating foreign financial institutions.  OFAC can prohibit or impose strict conditions on opening or maintaining, in the United States, a correspondent account or a payable-through account of a foreign financial institution that knowingly conducts or facilitates any significant transaction on behalf of a person who is designated pursuant to the relevant authority. The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List), but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law.  The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior.  For information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on Filing a Petition for Removal from an OFAC List . title: Remarks from Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent at the National Committee on U.S.-China Relations Gala
body: November 11, 2026 As prepared for delivery. Thank you, Evan [Greenberg], for that introduction, and for the invitation to be here. It gives me great pleasure to join you on this occasion. More than as representatives of the world’s largest economies, we meet tonight as stewards of one of this century’s most consequential relationships. Of course, when this Committee was formed in 1966, the Pacific was only the most visible distance between the United States and China. Formal diplomatic ties were still over a decade away. Our governments rarely spoke. And our people, likewise, rarely met. But a “small, loosely cohesive” band of China watchers believed that distance was reason to know more, not less. And so, they set out to understand China more deeply and to engage with it more seriously. They could not anticipate where exactly the relationship would lead, only that it would matter. The founders of this Committee set for themselves the ambitious task of reaching all segments of society—“from the layman, through the specialist, to the policy maker”—and “forging enduring links” between them. Tonight, sixty years later, take one look around this room, and you can see how fully their ambition has been realized. The United States and China represent different systems. Our national interests often diverge. But the links that you have built now bind generations and cultures together. They reach public servants and private citizens. Scholars who are bringing new ideas to light and entrepreneurs who are putting new ideas into practice. On both sides of the Pacific, people understand each other better because the National Committee on U.S.-China Relations brought them together. So, before I go any further, let me recognize two men who embody the best of this work. Steve Orlins has devoted much of his professional life to the U.S.-China relationship. He was part of the team that established diplomatic relations in the 1970s and then spent decades strengthening the ties that sustain them. Steve, you leave behind a legacy of great consequence, for which I offer my sincere thanks and congratulations. I am also pleased to acknowledge our second honoree. If Steve Orlins has shaped the history of our engagement with China, Stephen Schwarzman has made a transformative investment in its future. By founding the Schwarzman Scholars program, he has carried forward the conviction that animates this Committee. Relationships between nations are built on relationships between people. Steve, a new generation of leaders will be better prepared to navigate the U.S.-China relationship because you have given them the chance to understand it—and one another—more deeply. Congratulations. Now, while this Committee has supported bilateral relations for decades, the truth is that the ties between us span centuries. In fact, our relationship with China is nearly as old as the republic itself. In the winter of 1784, before we had a president—before we even had a constitution—an American ship, the Empress of China, departed New York Harbor and turned her bow toward the Pearl River. The vessel carried American crew and cargo, and with them, the confidence of a young country that had won its independence and was already reaching for a place among the great trading nations of the world. Major Samuel Shaw, who later served as the first American consul to China, recalled that upon the ship’s arrival, the Chinese people “were highly pleased at the prospect of so considerable a market for the productions of theirs.” Two nations, once separated by great distance, were drawn together by the possibilities of exchange. So before Washington and Beijing had ambassadors, we had merchants. Before our envoys learned how to engage, our people had already discovered how to do business. And before diplomacy gave this relationship its shape, the flow of goods gave it its force. Shaw celebrated that flow of commerce in both directions. And he was clear about the terms on which that commerce should proceed: “in all cases equal.” Even then, Americans expected a fair footing. Nearly two and a half centuries have passed since the Empress made her maiden voyage. What began with a single American ship bound for Canton—what began with the trading of ginseng for porcelain, tea, and silk—has matured into a vast trading network between the world’s two largest economies. Of course, the world that Samuel Shaw inhabited has long receded into history. But the instinct that carried him across an ocean endures. Americans still seek now what we sought then, which is to pursue opportunity wherever it lies, and to insist on fairness wherever we compete. Trade must advance the interests of both parties without diminishing the sovereignty of either. And it is precisely in that spirit that President Trump has approached our relationship with China. Today, U.S.-China relations are defined by the relationship between our two leaders. From the time of his first election, President Trump has, in his own words, “forged a friendship [with President Xi] built on mutual respect and the vital interests of our people.” That friendship has brought unprecedented direct engagement between the leaders of our two nations, which I try to extend to the working level. Of course, in May, President Trump traveled to Beijing. In September, President Xi came to Washington. And next week, I will join President Trump in Shenzhen, where the two leaders will meet before a fourth encounter in Miami. These meetings are historic in their frequency. Never before have our leaders engaged face-to-face so often in a single year. But more significant is the understanding they are helping to establish. President Trump and President Xi agree that the United States and China should build a constructive relationship on the basis of balance and reciprocity. And they’ve chartered two new institutions in service of those objectives. Under the Board of Trade, we reached consensus to identify more favorable tariff treatment for $30 billion of non-sensitive goods in each direction. The board also launched a working group to address trade barriers in the agricultural sector. And previously, China agreed to import at least 25 million metric tons of soybeans and 10 million metric tons of coal from the United States over the next two years. The Board of Investment, meanwhile, provides a structured forum for commercially meaningful issues, like market access for American companies and increased predictability for Chinese companies. And these initiatives are part of our broader work to advance a fair and reciprocal relationship with China. They give practical expression to the principle at the core of President Trump’s agenda, which is to measure the success of American engagement abroad by what it delivers here at home. By how it advances the prosperity of our people. Strengthens the resilience of our economy. And safeguards the security of our nation. Of course, the U.S. trade imbalance with China has long been a source of friction. And unlike a political class that tolerated China’s practices, President Trump has taken decisive steps to address them. Let me state firmly and unequivocally tonight that as we work toward a more balanced relationship, our objective is to de-risk, not to decouple. For decades, the American economy has grown too dependent on foreign supply, while China’s has become increasingly reliant on foreign demand. In other words, the United States must produce more of what we consume, while China must consume more of what it produces. Working together, we can strengthen both of our economies without perpetuating the imbalances between them. As Ray Dalio would say, we should have a big, beautiful rebalancing. So, as this President returns the American people to the center of American policy, let me be clear that our renewed emphasis on economic strength does not reflect hostility toward our trading partnerships. On the contrary, we are recovering the purpose that makes each of them worthwhile. After decades of imbalance, we are restoring a spirit of reciprocity for the benefit of both of our peoples. Now, as we work together to address the great questions of the last century, we must also summon the resolve to answer those of the next. In the final months of his life, Henry Kissinger was preoccupied with the challenges of a world he would not live to see. Even at the age of 100, his gaze, characteristically, was fixed on the future. On his last trip, he met with President Xi in Beijing to discuss deeper collaboration. Kissinger had come to believe that the advent of superintelligence could represent a novel class of strategic danger. And he recognized that the obligation of great nations, even—and perhaps especially—those with profound differences, is to find common purpose. So, at President Trump’s direction, we have begun that important work by establishing a new dialogue with China on SI, designed to guard against shared risks and prevent a misunderstanding between our two systems. We also expect to exchange best practices for evaluating and testing advanced models before their release, and for keeping human judgment firmly in command of this technology. Finally, we are establishing a direct channel to ensure that either nation can promptly alert the other to serious incidents involving its SI models. As SI advances, so will the need to engage in new areas of risk management—and to demonstrate how two nations can reconcile the demands of competition with the responsibilities of leadership. As we do so, we should harbor no illusions about the differences between the United States and China. As I stated earlier, our interests will not always coincide. And our approach to every challenge, likewise, will not always converge. Those early China watchers of the 1960s understood that the differences between our nations were too profound to ignore. But they also knew that the specter of our estrangement was too great to accept. Generations of leaders have demonstrated their faith in the value of this relationship, dating back to when those enterprising merchants aboard the Empress of China returned to New York Harbor. So I will take as my final words tonight those of Samuel Shaw, who, after a fourteen-month voyage, heralded “that a communication is thus happily opened between us and the Eastern Extreme of the Globe.” The patriots of 1784 opened that passage through commerce. The statesmen of the 1970s widened it through diplomacy. And for six decades, the men and women of this Committee have sustained it through the patient work of bringing our people together. Under President Trump, the United States will carry that work into a new era. We will enlarge the prospects for prosperity on both sides of the Pacific. And, secure in our own strength and unwavering commitment to the American people, we will honor those who first forged this relationship by renewing our resolve to strengthen it. Thank you and congratulations. ###

title: November 9, 2026 - FDA Approves First Factor Xla Inhibitor to Help Prevent Stroke in Certain Adults at High Risk
body: FDA News Release FDA Approves First Factor Xla Inhibitor to Help Prevent Stroke in Certain Adults at High Risk For Immediate Release: November 09, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved Sunharbo (asundexian) 50 mg tablets, the first factor XIa (FXIa) inhibitor for use in combination with antiplatelet therapy to reduce the risk of stroke in adults following a recent mild-to-moderate non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke (a stroke caused by a clot that did not originate in the heart) or a high-risk transient ischemic attack (TIA), often called a “mini-stroke.” “Stroke is a leading cause of disability and death in the United States, and survivors are at risk of having another stroke,” said Hylton V. Joffe, M.D., MMSc, Director of the Office of Cardiology, Hematology, Endocrinology, and Nephrology in the FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research . “Today’s approval represents a meaningful advance for patients and health care providers seeking a new option for secondary stroke prevention.” The effectiveness of Sunharbo was demonstrated in the OCEANIC-STROKE study , a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 study that enrolled 12,327 adults. Participants had a recent non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke (NIH Stroke Scale ≤15) or high-risk TIA and were randomly assigned to Sunharbo or placebo within 72 hours of symptom onset. Both groups also received antiplatelet therapy. Sunharbo 50 mg once daily significantly reduced the risk of ischemic stroke by 26% compared to placebo over a median treatment of 14.2 months. The overall rate of major bleeding was similar between the Sunharbo and placebo groups but was increased with Sunharbo in patients older than 75 years and during the first 90 days of treatment. Gastrointestinal bleeding occurred more commonly with Sunharbo compared to placebo. The most frequently reported adverse reaction (occurring in 3% or greater of Sunharbo-treated patients) was diarrhea. Concomitant use with medicines that are combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inducers (such as carbamazepine) is not recommended because these medicines may decrease Sunharbo’s effectiveness. Sunharbo is not recommended in patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment. Sunharbo should be withheld at least 24 hours before elective surgery or invasive procedures and for at least 24 hours after thrombolysis for acute ischemic stroke. Sunharbo is not approved for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation. The FDA granted Sunharbo Fast Track and Priority Review designations. The approval was granted to Bayer HealthCare Pharmaceuticals Inc., Whippany, N.J. November 5, 2026 - FDA Grants Accelerated Approval to a New Treatment for Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
body: FDA News Release FDA Grants Accelerated Approval to a New Treatment for Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma For Immediate Release: November 05, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today granted accelerated approval to Rybrevant Faspro (amivantamab and hyaluronidase-lpuj) for the treatment of adults with recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) whose disease has progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy. HNSCC is an aggressive, life-threatening disease for which there is a high unmet need for effective therapies. Rybrevant Faspro is not indicated as a treatment for patients with oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma that is associated with human papillomavirus (HPV). Approval was based on trial results showing that more than double the percentage of patients responded to the drug compared to currently approved therapies. This is the first approval in 10 years of a drug for patients with recurrent or metastatic HNSCC who had received prior platinum-based chemotherapy. “Today’s approval represents a meaningful step forward for patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, a disease where treatment options have historically been limited and outcomes remain poor,” said Angelo De Claro, M.D., director of the FDA’s Oncology Center of Excellence . “This therapy offers patients and their physicians a new option with the potential to make a real difference in people’s lives.” The Accelerated Approval Program allows for earlier approval of drugs that treat serious conditions and fill an unmet medical need based on surrogate or intermediate endpoints. In this case, accelerated approval of Rybrevant Faspro was granted based on overall response rate and duration of response. Since it is not yet confirmed whether this will translate into a clinically meaningful benefit in long-term outcomes, the FDA has required confirmatory studies to verify and describe clinical benefit. In an open-label, multicenter clinical trial involving 102 patients with recurrent or metastatic HNSCC, Rybrevant Faspro had an overall response rate of 42%, meaning these patients saw their tumor either decrease in size or disappear. Of those patients who had a response, 56% had a response lasting six months or longer. Currently approved therapies are associated with an overall response rate of around 20% or less and poor outcomes. The prescribing information for use as a single agent includes warnings and precautions for hypersensitivity and administration-related reactions, interstitial lung disease (ILD)/pneumonitis, dermatologic adverse reactions, ocular toxicity, and harm to an unborn baby. The FDA granted Rybrevant Faspro Breakthrough Therapy designation for this indication. The approval was granted to Janssen Biotech, Inc. title: November 2, 2026 - FDA Provides Clarity to Support Cell and Gene Therapy Development and Quality
body: FDA News Release FDA Provides Clarity to Support Cell and Gene Therapy Development and Quality FDA issues final guidance for cell and gene therapy manufacturers, recommends building potency assurance into every stage of a therapy’s lifecycle — from early development through patient delivery For Immediate Release: November 02, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today issued final guidance for manufacturers of cellular and gene therapy (CGT) products to implement a comprehensive, science- and risk-based plan for making sure their products meet potency standards. The guidance provides FDA’s recommendations for a Potency Assurance Strategy, which guides manufacturers to test and verify — before a product reaches a patient — that every batch meets a defined standard of potency to do what the product is supposed to do therapeutically. The Potency Assurance for Cellular and Gene Therapy Products final guidance replaces FDA's 2011 potency testing guidance for CGT products and applies to treatments for serious and often life-threatening conditions. By law, manufacturers are expected to verify that their products work as intended, from the time of approval through post-approval monitoring. This final guidance provides FDA’s current thinking and recommendations on how manufacturers can meet that requirement. "Patients who receive cellular and gene therapies are often battling serious or life-threatening conditions, such as cancers and rare diseases, and they deserve the assurance that the product administered to them will perform as intended," said Karim Mikhail, B. Pharm., M.S., Director of the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research . "This guidance reflects the FDA's commitment to ensuring America remains the best place in the world to innovate — and that innovation is matched by the highest standards of product quality and patient safety." The guidance provides flexible, risk-based recommendations for manufacturers on how to integrate potency considerations at every stage of development and commercialization — from early-phase investigational new drug (IND) submissions through biologics license application (BLA) approval and continued post-market verification. Key topics include controls for variability in raw materials, testing during manufacturing, and lab tests that confirm each batch is biologically active in a way that matches its intended therapeutic effect. The guidance also addresses specialized considerations for products with short shelf lives, viral vector gene therapies, and patient-specific therapies. By giving manufacturers a clear, predictable roadmap, this guidance supports faster access to safe and effective therapies for patients who often have no other treatment options — many of whom receive products made individually for a single person. In doing so, it advances the FDA's public health pillars: protecting patients through rigorous quality standards, promoting innovation by providing regulatory clarity, and reinforcing the integrity of the supply chain for some of the most complex medical products in existence. The FDA will host a webinar on December 10, 2026, to help stakeholders understand and implement the guidance. title: October 30, 2026 - FDA Approves First Plasmid DNA-based Immunotherapy for Adults with Recurrent Respiratory Papillomatosis
body: FDA News Release FDA Approves First Plasmid DNA-based Immunotherapy for Adults with Recurrent Respiratory Papillomatosis Groundbreaking therapy provides additional treatment option that fights the disease at its source, not only its symptoms For Immediate Release: October 30, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today granted accelerated approval for Voceryq (doruxapapogene ralaplasmid and lalikinogene sifuplasmid-gxfd) for treatment of adults with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP), a rare disease caused by human papillomavirus (HPV) that leads to the formation of small, wart-like growths in the patient’s airways. This approval, the first for a plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy in the U.S., offers patients a new therapeutic option that targets the root cause of RRP and has been shown to reduce the burden of surgical intervention, representing an important step forward for a patient population with limited treatment options. “Adults living with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis often face an exhausting and relentless cycle of repeated surgeries, managing their disease, but never truly escaping it. Today’s approval represents a meaningful scientific breakthrough: a plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy that harnesses the body’s own immune system to fight the underlying cause of RRP,” said Karim Mikhail, B. Pharm., M.S., Director of the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER) . “For patients, that could mean fewer surgeries, fewer disruptions, and more time living their lives on their own terms. The FDA is proud to help bring that possibility within reach.” The agency based this accelerated approval on clinical trial data showing Voceryq helps reduce the frequency of surgical procedures required to remove growths in adult patients with RRP — an intermediate clinical endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit. The accelerated approval pathway allows the FDA to approve drugs or biologics for serious or life-threatening conditions based on an effect on a surrogate or intermediate clinical endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit. The manufacturer must conduct post-approval clinical trials to verify and describe Voceryq’s clinical benefit. RRP is a rare, chronic disease in which wart-like growths caused by HPV types 6 and/or 11 form in the airways, most often around the larynx (voice box), particularly the vocal cords. These growths, called papillomas, can cause symptoms like hoarseness, chronic cough, and voice changes, and in severe cases can spread to other parts of the respiratory tract, causing difficulty breathing. While surgery can remove the growths, there is no cure, and the virus persists in the tissue even after the growths are removed, so patients often need repeated procedures over many years. In some cases, RRP carries a risk of becoming cancerous over time. Voceryq is a recombinant plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy that delivers two plasmids (small pieces of DNA originally derived from bacteria) into the body’s cells, one of which contains the genetic instructions for specific HPV proteins and the other an immune response-enhancing molecule called IL-12. The therapy is designed to stimulate the immune system to respond to and attack cells infected by the specific types of HPV that cause RRP (types 6 and 11).  Voceryq is administered via intramuscular (IM) injection using the CELLECTRA 5PSP Device, which delivers the dose and facilitates electroporation, a technique which uses brief electrical pulses to temporarily and reversibly create pores in the cell membranes to enable the delivery of Voceryq into the body’s cells. The safety and effectiveness of Voceryq was evaluated in an open-label multicenter clinical trial in 32 adults diagnosed with RRP. Eligible patients had two or more surgeries to remove laryngotracheal papillomas in the 12 months prior to Voceryq treatment, including a scheduled surgery at trial entry. Seven (27%) out of 26 patients who had at least three baseline surgeries did not require any surgery intervention during the first year after treatment. The most commonly reported adverse reactions to Voceryq were injection site reactions, headache, fatigue, hypertension (high blood pressure), nausea, and dizziness. Adverse effects associated with the electroporation technique may include brief muscle contractions or tetany, temporary bleeding at the administration site, anxiety, vasovagal reactions including lightheadedness and dizziness, transient changes in creatine phosphokinase, erythema (skin redness) at the injection site, and pain at the injection site. The FDA granted Voceryq Breakthrough and Orphan Drug designations. The FDA granted accelerated approval of Voceryq to Inovio Pharmaceuticals, Inc. October 22, 2026 - FDA Launches New Program to Advance Neuroscience Medical Product Development
body: FDA News Release FDA Launches New Program to Advance Neuroscience Medical Product Development Neuroscience Advancement and Innovation Nexus to coordinate agency action on brain and nervous system conditions, with inaugural focus on Alzheimer's prevention For Immediate Release: October 22, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today announced the launch of the Neuroscience Advancement and Innovation Nexus (NAIN) , a new agency program aligned with the Trump Administration’s efforts to accelerate medical innovation and deliver breakthrough treatments. NAIN is designed to advance the science, tools, and regulatory approaches needed to support the development of medical products for conditions affecting the brain and nervous system. NAIN’s inaugural initiative, the Alzheimer's Prevention Accelerator , will focus on advancing medical products that help delay or prevent Alzheimer's disease. Both efforts support the National Alzheimer’s Project Act (NAPA), the federal government's comprehensive roadmap for coordinated action on Alzheimer's and related dementias. "The launch of NAIN reflects FDA's commitment — in support of the Trump Administration’s drive to transform health care innovation — to making sure our regulatory science and cross-center collaboration keep pace with the rapid advances happening in neuroscience," said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas, J.D. "Through NAIN and the Alzheimer's Prevention Accelerator, we are bringing the full breadth of FDA's expertise to bear on one of the most urgent public health challenges of our time.” Developing medical products for neuroscience indications is associated with complex scientific and clinical challenges, including limited understanding of underlying biology, variable disease presentation, and difficulties in demonstrating meaningful clinical benefit, particularly for conditions that develop over many years. Advances in biomarkers, digital health technologies, and other medical product development tools, however, offer important opportunities to address these challenges. NAIN will bring together scientific and regulatory expertise from the FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, and Center for Devices and Radiological Health to address scientific and regulatory questions that benefit from coordinated consideration across drugs, biologics, and devices. NAIN will encompass conditions that affect the brain and nervous system broadly, including neurologic and psychiatric disorders, substance use disorders, and pain. NAIN will also support robust engagement with patients, industry, academia and other stakeholders to advance these efforts. As its first initiative, NAIN is launching the Alzheimer's Prevention Accelerator . This inaugural initiative will draw on perspectives from across the FDA and engage patients and caregivers, researchers, industry, public-private partnerships and other government agencies. The initiative will explore innovative approaches to advancing clinical trials for Alzheimer’s disease prevention and early-intervention drug development with emphasis on trial populations, stage-appropriate endpoints, and evidentiary approaches for demonstrating prevention or delay of cognitive decline due to Alzheimer’s disease. The FDA has long been committed to supporting the development of safe and effective medical products that address diseases and conditions of the brain and nervous system. Through NAIN and the Alzheimer's Prevention Accelerator, the agency is taking a proactive, coordinated approach to accelerating progress, bringing together its scientific and regulatory expertise, engaging the broader research and development community, and working in concert with federal partners to meet the scale of this public health challenge. title: October 20, 2026 - FDA Issues Final Guidance on Prescription Drug Apps and Software
body: FDA News Release FDA Issues Final Guidance on Prescription Drug Apps and Software New policy clarifies when app content requires FDA review and how drug-connected software must be described on medication labels For Immediate Release: October 20, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today released final guidance establishing a clear framework for how drug companies can develop, distribute, and label apps used alongside their prescription medicines. The guidance ends longstanding uncertainty by providing recommendations about when app content is subject to FDA submission requirements, when an app should be mentioned on a drug’s official label, and what companies should submit to the agency. “Mobile apps are playing a growing role in how patients manage their medications and health conditions,” said Captain Chris Wheeler, Pharm.D., Director of the Division of Medical Policy Programs within FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research . “This guidance helps ensure that the information these tools provide is accurate, evidence-based, and clearly communicated to both patients and their providers.” The guidance addresses three key questions for industry: when app content is treated as FDA-required labeling versus promotional labeling, when an app should be referenced in a drug’s official prescribing information, and what companies should submit to FDA when they distribute app content to users. The guidance identifies two categories of companion software: Apps connected to a medical device (such as an app paired with an asthma inhaler) generally should be described on the drug’s official prescribing label, given the central role the software plays in how the medicine is used. Standalone apps (such as symptom trackers, dose reminders, or health coaching tools) should appear on the prescribing label if the company can show the app is essential for safe and effective use or can demonstrate a meaningful clinical benefit. In most cases, content a companion app displays to users will be treated as promotional material, consistent with how the FDA handles other drug advertising. “This guidance reflects FDA’s commitment to responsible, risk-proportionate oversight of digital health, an area that is a key priority for the agency and is evolving rapidly and holds significant promise for improving patient care,” said Michael Davis, M.D., Ph.D., Director of the FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research . “By aligning our approach across drug and device centers, we are giving developers a clear and consistent pathway to bring safe, effective digital health technologies to patients.” “Companion apps are quickly moving beyond simple dose reminders toward tools that adapt to each patient,” said Jared Seehafer, M.S., FDA Deputy Commissioner for Technology . “Finalizing this guidance gives drug companies and their technology partners a stable foundation to build on as these technologies advance and helps ensure patients and providers can trust the information they receive.” This guidance also reflects the FDA’s ongoing commitment to modernizing its regulatory framework to keep pace with rapidly evolving digital health technologies. By providing clear, practical recommendations for both drug-connected software and standalone software, the agency aims to reduce unnecessary uncertainty for developers and manufacturers while preserving the safety and effectiveness standards that patients and healthcare providers rely on. The final guidance is available here . title: October 20, 2026 - FDA Approves First-of-Its-Kind Chronic Hepatitis B Treatment
body: FDA News Release FDA Approves First-of-Its-Kind Chronic Hepatitis B Treatment New treatment may allow some patients to maintain viral control after stopping all hepatitis B therapy For Immediate Release: October 20, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved Hibsago (bepirovirsen) injection, in combination with existing antiviral therapy, to treat chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in certain adults without cirrhosis. Hibsago is the first FDA-approved antisense oligonucleotide to treat chronic hepatitis B. Hibsago is approved for certain adults without cirrhosis who have been taking HBV antiviral therapy for at least six months, have suppressed levels of HBV in their blood and have hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) levels of 3,000 IU/mL or less, as determined by an FDA-authorized test. “For many people living with chronic hepatitis B, treatment can mean taking antiviral medication for years to keep the virus suppressed,” said Wendy Carter, DO, Acting Director of the Office of Infectious Diseases in the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research . “Hibsago provides a new treatment approach that gives some patients the possibility of maintaining control of the virus after all chronic HBV treatment has ended. This approval represents an important advance for people living with this serious disease.” Chronic hepatitis B is a long-term liver infection caused by HBV. Over time, the infection can lead to serious liver disease, including cirrhosis, and increase the risk of liver cancer. Hibsago works by targeting the genetic instructions the virus uses to make copies of itself and viral proteins, helping reduce the amount of virus and hepatitis B surface antigen in the body. The FDA also authorized the Roche Elecsys HBsAg II quant II RxDx assay as a companion diagnostic device to aid in the selection of patients with chronic HBV infection for treatment with antiviral therapy in accordance with the FDA approved drug labeling and to assist in monitoring patients throughout the course of treatment. Researchers studied Hibsago in two clinical trials that compared it with a placebo, an inactive treatment. Hibsago is injected under the skin for up to 24 weeks. Patients take it alongside their existing hepatitis B medicine and continue that medicine for at least 24 weeks after their last Hibsago injection. Some patients may then be able to stop their existing medicine if they meet certain health and lab test requirements. Across the two trials, 24% of patients who received Hibsago met the requirements to stop their existing medicine, compared with none who received placebo. Twenty-four weeks after stopping all hepatitis B treatment, 19% of patients who received Hibsago still had the virus under control, and a protein that signals hepatitis B infection (HBsAg) could not be detected in their blood. Hibsago has a boxed warning for serious liver reactions as well as low platelet counts, which can increase the risk of potentially life-threatening bleeding. Hibsago also has warnings for worsening kidney function, serious inflammatory adverse reactions like vasculitis, and serious risks if the injection is not administered properly. Patients need regular blood tests and follow up with their healthcare provider before and during treatment to monitor these risks. The most common side effects, excluding laboratory abnormalities, are injection site reactions, fever, fatigue and headache. The FDA granted Hibsago Fast Track and Breakthrough Therapy designations as well as Priority Review . The approval was granted to GSK plc. Media: FDA Request for Comment 202-690-6343 Consumer: 888-INFO-FDA The FDA, an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines and other biological products for human use, and medical devices. The agency also is responsible for the safety and security of our nation’s food supply, cosmetics, dietary supplements, radiation-emitting electronic products, and for regulating tobacco products. ###
